question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only coverage: daridorexant in pregnancy

These are navigation counts only. They are not comparable across sources and do not establish safety, evidence quality, clinical applicability, or study findings.

| Source | Count | What the count indicates | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** | **3** | Three records matched the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy search. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | The records may not represent distinct studies, human pregnancy studies, or reported pregnancy outcomes. The count does not establish study quality or findings. The returned query also noted that the daridorexant MeSH term was not found. |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** | **4** | Four registration records matched the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy query. [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) | Registration does not establish enrollment, posted results, outcomes, or confirmed applicability to pregnant participants. |
| **DailyMed** | **1** | One name-matched product-label record was found. [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) | It does not establish pregnancy-specific evidence, independent clinical evidence, current approval status, or applicability of a particular formulation. |
| **LactMed** | **Not applicable** | LactMed is a lactation-only resource. | This is not a pregnancy search result and cannot establish pregnancy or general pediatric evidence. [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** | **0 rows; 0 distinct PMIDs** | No literal daridorexant drug-name row match was found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot, dated **2026-11-17**. [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) | This does not prove that relevant research is absent elsewhere. The returned MPRINT count reflects literal drug-name matching in selected snapshot tables; it is not a full-portal search, does not perform name resolution, and rows are not necessarily distinct studies. |

**Bottom line:** The count-only lookup found potentially relevant records in PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and DailyMed, but it did not retrieve or assess their narratives, populations, study sizes, outcomes, or pregnancy applicability. LactMed was not applicable to the requested population, and MPRINT had no literal Gold-snapshot row match. No source-level safety conclusion can be drawn from these counts; an empty or non-applicable result is not proof of drug identity, safety, or absence of evidence elsewhere.

The lookup also reported that it did not identify a curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed in its prototype source review; that is a limitation of the lookup, not proof that no such resource exists.
